North Atlantic Track

A published daily route system over the North Atlantic, providing organized and coordinated tracks for transatlantic flights to maximize safety and efficiency.

Questions and answers

Questions and answers

What is North Atlantic Track?

In this glossary, North Atlantic Track refers to: A published daily route system over the North Atlantic, providing organized and coordinated tracks for transatlantic flights to maximize safety and efficiency.

How is North Atlantic Track used in aviation?

In aviation communication, this term appears in contexts such as: "Cleared via North Atlantic Track Charlie, report entry and exit points, maintain assigned Mach number."

Why does North Atlantic Track matter in aviation?

North Atlantic Track matters because it supports clear communication in Navigation contexts for Pilots, Air Traffic Controllers, and Cabin Crew. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as ICAO Level 4, ICAO Level 5, ICAO Level 6, and EASA FCL.055.

Who uses North Atlantic Track?

North Atlantic Track is mainly used by Pilots, Air Traffic Controllers, and Cabin Crew.

What category does North Atlantic Track belong to?

In this glossary, North Atlantic Track is grouped under Navigation. Related pages in this category explain adjacent procedures, commands and operational concepts.

Where does this definition come from?

This definition is sourced from ICAO Doc 9432, FAA PCG and published by Protermify Aviation as a static aviation reference page.
